title: evidence_refs validator inconsistency — SSoT advertises finding-id form but kernel's _check_agent_ref rejects bare ids
raised_by: ARIA-V10.4 full endurance cycle 3 (cyc-20260520T131453Z-auto, round-2 primary plan, real-Claude, post-F-019 fix)
resolved_by: ARIA-V10.4 Phase 3.H.9 (SSoT evidence_refs guidance harmonized with strict file-path validator)

evidence.v10_4_closure_confirmed: cycle 3 reached CROSS_REVIEWED state, cross_review_recorded fired for both p2c + c2p directions. F-016/F-017/F-018/F-019 architecturally closed in production. F-020 is a POST-closure failure on the Round-2 revision pipeline.

validator_inconsistency._valid_evidence_ref (plan_convergence.py: accepts FINDING_ID_RE (severity-tagged, e.g. ORPHAN-HIGH-082) OR file path
validator_inconsistency._check_agent_ref (evidence_validator.py:: accepts file path ONLY, file must exist at workspace SHA
validator_inconsistency.FINDING_ID_RE (plan_convergence.py:20): ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)*-(CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW)-[0-9]{3,}$ — requires severity token; bare F-NNN does NOT match
validator_inconsistency.consequence: An agent that follows the SSoT's 'OR a finding-id' guidance writes bare F-019 into satisfaction_matrix[].evidence_refs and is rejected at the existence-validator layer with agent_evidence_path_missing.
validator_inconsistency.ssot_drift_evidence: primary-planner.md:19 says 'concrete repo paths at file:line resolution — the ONLY admissible evidence', but layer-2-aria-canonical-envelope.md:29 said evidence_refs accept 'OR a finding-id (ORPHAN-HIGH-082, F-014)'. The two SSoT layers disagreed; the strict layer is canonical.

structural_root_cause.ssot_internal_inconsistency: layer-2-aria-canonical-envelope.md (the canonical envelope SSoT) advertised finding-id as a valid evidence_refs entry, but the kernel's existence-validator (evidence_validator._check_agent_ref) only accepts paths that resolve to real files. The discrepancy was invisible until a Round-2 primary planner — instructed by the cross-reviewer to 'tightly anchor evidence' — chose the finding-id form for findings it had just emitted.
structural_root_cause.lesson: Evidence references cross two validator layers (shape-validator at plan_convergence._valid_evidence_ref + existence-validator at evidence_validator._check_agent_ref). Documentation MUST reflect the STRICTEST validator. The previous SSoT documented the shape-validator's looser rule and silently misled agents that emitted refs flowing through the strict validator.
structural_root_cause.tier_1_anchor: Same drift class as F-018 (envelope shape) and F-019 (risk entry shape) — at each kernel-contract surface, the documentation must mirror the strictest enforcement layer, not the loosest. SSoT-drift is the recurring failure pattern.

tier_1_architectural_fix.scope: SSoT correction — harmonize layer-2 evidence_refs guidance with the strict existence-validator
files_changed: .claude/knowledge/layer-2-aria-canonical-envelope.md (line 29 — replaced misleading 'OR a finding-id' with explicit 'use aria-findings/F-NNN.json[:<line>] path form'; named the validator function _check_agent_ref so agents + operators trace the rejection class to source)
aria-kernel/tests/invariants/v10/test_phase_v10_4_phase_3_h_9_evidence_refs_path_only.py (Tier-3 invariant — assertion that the SSoT's evidence_refs row does NOT advertise bare finding-id form)
tier_1_architectural_fix.tier_rationale: Tier-1 (make impossible): SSoT now matches the strictest enforcement layer (_check_agent_ref). An agent following the SSoT cannot produce an evidence_ref that fails the existence-validator. Tier-3 (make detectable): invariant test asserts the SSoT's evidence_refs row never re-advertises bare finding-id form, catching documentation regression at CI time.

kernel_code_changes: NONE — kernel validators were already correct and were structurally stricter than the SSoT promised. The fix harmonizes the SSoT down to the kernel's actual contract.
deferred_to_v10_5: OPTIONAL: extend _check_agent_ref to ALSO accept finding-ids by resolving them to aria-findings/{id}.json. This would make the two validator layers self-consistent at the relaxed end (instead of at the strict end). Trade-off: more kernel surface vs. operator-friendly finding-id evidence form. Not in V10.4 scope because (a) the SSoT-only fix already unblocks cycle 4+ and (b) the existing bare F-NNN finding-id format would still need FINDING_ID_RE relaxation, which compounds scope.

expected_impact_on_endurance.before_fix: cycle 3 round-2 primary rejected at evidence_validator; subsequent cycles' round-2 revisions also reject when cross-reviewer demands tighter evidence anchoring. The cross_review_recorded transition succeeds (V10.4 closure confirmed) but the cycle never reaches CONVERGED or implementation_requested.
expected_impact_on_endurance.after_fix: next round-2 primary subprocess hot-reloads the updated SSoT via knowledge anchor at aria-primary-planner.md:44. Round-2 evidence_refs cite findings via aria-findings/F-NNN.json[:line] path form → existence-validator accepts → state transitions to either CONVERGED or HUMAN_REQUIRED with real verdict.
